newsitem.title: FRANCE: France to set Thomson-CSF sale terms soon.
newsitem.headline: France to set Thomson-CSF sale terms soon.

text.p: The French government will decide in the coming days on the sale terms of a 58 percent stake in defence electronics group Thomson-CSF, including whether it will be done in a private placement or through a public sale.
Official sources said on Wednesday that "the government will announce in the next few days the terms of the privatisation of Thomson-CSF."

The sources added that the constitutional court, the Conseil d'Etat, would rule on Friday whether the government should follow a 1986 privatisation law for the sale and not another 1991 law which could have speeded up the sale.

The government has decided to sell the stake in Thomson-CSF as soon as possible, probably in early 1997, while delaying the sale of the wholly owned consumer electronics branch Thomson Multimedia (TMM).
The government on December 4 suspended the planned privatisation sale of Thomson SA -- the state company which owns 58 percent of Thomson-CSF and all of TMM -- to Lagardere Groupe.
It did so after the independent Privatisation Commission objected to the terms of the planned sale of TMM by Lagardere to Daewoo Electronics of South Korea.
